transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lucas Ferreira (CTO - Zenvia), Ana Costa (Lead ML Eng - Zenvia), Marcos Silva (Platform PM - Zenvia)

Topics: SDKs + LangChain/LlamaIndex integration, gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits/quotas, observability/tracing hooks, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs

00:00 Lucas: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got a packed agenda. We're evaluating Redwood to handle a set of LLM features inside our customer support pipeline and sms flows, so want to understand integration points.
00:14 Maya: Great, Lucas, thanks. Quick intros, then Ravi will go over the technical integration surface.
00:22 Ravi: Hi team, I'll keep it practical. First question: are you planning to use Redwood Hosted API or considering Dedicated/Private from the start?
00:33 Lucas: For PoC, hosted is fine, but if latency and data controls look good we may want Dedicated for predictable throughput and later Private for regulated accounts.
00:41 Ana: We also use LangChain and some LlamaIndex-based retrieval stacks, so SDK compatibility and examples matter to us.
00:52 Ravi: Totally - we have official SDKs in Python/Node and sample connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. There are example agents and retrieval-augmented generation notebooks. I'll share those after the call.
01:05 Marcos: How are we supposed to route requests? We have an internal API gateway and also run an envoy sidecar pattern in k8s. Do you recommend connecting Redwood directly from our services or proxying through our gateway?
01:18 Ravi: Both are supported. For hosted, many customers route via a small gateway/proxy that handles auth and rate-limiting at the edge; others call Redwood directly from backend services. For Dedicated/Private, you can install an internal connector or configure the private control plane inside your VPC.
01:36 Ana: Any constraints on network egress or TLS? We need mTLS to our proxy ideally.
01:43 Ravi: We support TLS 1.2/1.3 and can integrate with customer-managed TLS termination. For Private deployments we can work with your infra to set up mutual TLS or direct peering. There may be a small ops window to exchange certs.
02:05 Lucas: On rate limits - currently we expect bursty traffic, maybe 200-300 rps at peak for inference calls, and we'd need soft QoS. What are typical quotas for Hosted vs Dedicated?
02:22 Maya: Hosted has per-account quotas by default - you can request quota increases. Dedicated gives you reserved throughput with predictable concurrency and SLOs. For POCs we often suggest a small burst allocation and then a Dedicated pilot if you need guaranteed throughput.
02:39 Ravi: Also, we expose headers for quotas and usage in responses and have backoff guidance in the SDKs. If you want to enforce stricter limits we recommend placing a gateway in front to handle token-level throttling or per-route quotas.
03:02 Ana: Does the SDK give hooks for retry/backoff and instrumentation?
03:10 Ravi: Yes - SDKs include retry middleware, pluggable backoff strategies, and simple hooks for request/response interceptors so you can emit traces to your APM. We have a tracing integration doc for Datadog/NewRelic and sample code for pushing token-level metrics.
03:28 Marcos: Observability is huge for us. We need per-route latency, token counts, and model-level error rates, and export to our prometheus/grafana stack.
03:40 Ravi: We expose per-request metrics and token accounting via response metadata. For Hosted, those metrics are visible in Redwood Console; you can also stream logs or push metrics via webhooks. For Private, you can integrate directly into your internal telemetry pipeline and even forward traces to Prometheus exporters.
03:59 Lucas: Can you show a quick example of how a LangChain chain would call Redwood?
04:06 Ravi: Sure - (Ravi shares quick high-level snippet) The SDK offers a LangChain LLM wrapper - you pass in an api_key and model name, and the wrapper handles streaming and callbacks. There's a LlamaIndex connector pattern too, for indexing and retrieval.
04:28 Ana: We've seen some connectors call the API synchronously and lose streaming behaviour. Does your LangChain wrapper support streaming tokens to the client?
04:38 Ravi: Yes - streaming is supported end-to-end. The LangChain wrapper exposes the streaming callback hooks; you'll get partial tokens if you want to render incremental UI. Note: some community connectors may not wire streaming correctly - use our official examples.
04:58 Marcos: About data retention and logs: for hosted, will Redwood keep transcripts? We need to ensure retention and deletion policies for PII.
05:08 Maya: By default Hosted retains logs and request metadata per privacy policy but can opt-out of retention for enterprise accounts. Dedicated and Private give you control - logs can be stored in your infra or set to short retention. We'll send security docs with the exact retention controls.
05:25 Lucas: And KMS integration? We use AWS KMS and HSM for key management.
05:30 Ravi: We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private; Hosted can integrate with KMS via bring-your-own-key for certain packages. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
05:44 Ana: If we run a proxy route do we need to do anything special for the KV cache behavior? We rely on prefix caching for cost savings.
05:54 Ravi: Caching and KV cache are runtime features in the Redwood serving layer; if you proxy requests make sure the proxy passes full context headers and doesn't re-truncate prompts. For shared caches across instances, Dedicated has consistent KV management; Hosted caches are regional but consistent for the same account.
06:18 Marcos: Do you support model variants automatically? Eg fallback to a quantized variant if capacity is constrained?
06:25 Ravi: Yes - smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants based on policy. You can configure routing by latency/cost/region and have automatic fallback. We'll include routing policy docs.
06:40 Lucas: Security reviews - we'll need SOC2 and network diagrams for procurement.
06:45 Maya: We'll send SOC2 reports and the security whitepaper. For Private deployments we provide architecture diagrams and options for air-gapped installs.
06:57 Ana: On latency targets: our 95th pctl needs to be under 250ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens). Can Redwood meet that on Hosted?
07:08 Ravi: Typical short prompt latencies vary by model; for small/medium models Hosted can meet ~150-300ms under light load, but Dedicated with pinned capacity will be much more predictable. For strict 250ms at scale, Dedicated or on-prem is recommended.
07:27 Lucas: For the pilot, what's a reasonable scope and timeline?
07:33 Maya: Many customers do a 2-4 week PoC: integrate SDK + LangChain examples, run sample traffic, validate latency and cost. Then we size Dedicated capacity for month 2 if needed.
07:46 Marcos: Costing - can you provide a sample calculation for token cost vs Dedicated reserved GPU hours?
07:53 Maya: Yes, we'll provide pilot pricing and a simple cost model spreadsheet.
08:02 Ana: One more - anyone here tried integrating LlamaIndex with your retrieval? We've had index staleness issues when using external vector DBs.
08:12 Ravi: We have examples for LlamaIndex + vector DBs and recommended sync/ttl patterns to avoid staleness. For high turnover data, sync frequency and small snapshot windows help.
08:28 Lucas: Any mention of vendor lock-in concerns from ops? Our infra team worries about migrating away later.
08:36 Maya: We try to minimize lock-in - SDKs are standard HTTP plus open model support and exportable configurations. Dedicated/Private give you more portability since models and configs can be pinned.
08:50 Ana: OK this is helpful.
09:00 (brief cross talk)
09:15 Maya: Recap - we'll send SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, security docs, pilot pricing and schedule the technical deep-dive.
09:27 Lucas: Sounds good. We'll circulate internal stakeholders and aim to have sample volumes by end of week.
09:35 Marcos: Let's set the deep-dive with infra and networking. 60 minutes to go over proxy, mTLS and rate-limits.
09:43 Maya: I'll propose times for 2026-05-11.
09:49 Lucas: Great, thanks everyone.
09:53 End of recording
